name: TJA1051T_3_1J
title: High-speed CAN transceiver
summary: A transceiver for high-speed automotive CAN networks: it turns a CAN controller's TXD and RXD into the differential CANH/CANL bus and back, with timing guaranteed for CAN FD up to 5 Mbit/s. It runs from 5 V with Normal and Silent modes selected on pin S. Pin 5 sets the version: unconnected (TJA1051T), a VIO logic supply for 3 V to 5 V microcontrollers (TJA1051T/3 in SO8, TJA1051TK/3 in HVSON8) or an enable for a low-current Off mode (TJA1051T/E). Protection covers TXD dominant time-out, undervoltage on VCC and VIO, overtemperature and ±58 V on the bus pins.
key_figures: up to 5 Mbit/s in the CAN FD fast phase
5 mA typ recessive, 50 mA typ dominant
40 ns to 250 ns (VIO versions), 220 ns max (others)

circuits.title: Typical application of the TJA1051T/E
circuits.description: A 5 V node. Battery feeds a 5 V regulator through a series diode; the regulator output carries a polarised bulk capacitor and supplies both the transceiver's VCC, decoupled by a capacitor at the pin, and the microcontroller's VDD. The microcontroller drives EN and S from two port pins, sends on TXD from its TX0 and reads RXD on RX0. CANH and CANL leave for the bus through a split termination: two resistors in series across the pair, with a capacitor from their midpoint to ground.

circuits.title: Typical application of the TJA1051T/3 or TJA1051TK/3
circuits.description: A node whose microcontroller runs from 3 V. Battery passes a series diode to two regulators. The 3 V regulator, with a polarised bulk capacitor on its output, supplies the microcontroller's VDD and the transceiver's VIO, which has its own capacitor at the pin. The 5 V regulator, also with a polarised bulk capacitor, supplies VCC, decoupled at the pin; its enable input may be driven from a microcontroller port pin. The microcontroller drives S, sends on TXD and reads RXD at 3 V levels. The bus side carries the same split termination as the 5 V node.
notes: The link from Pxx to the 5 V regulator's enable is optional.
The TJA1051TK/3 in HVSON8 takes the same connections.

circuits.title: Timing test circuit
circuits.description: The part runs from +5 V with 47 µF and 100 nF to ground. A signal drives TXD; RXD is loaded by 15 pF to ground; RL and 100 pF in parallel sit across CANH and CANL. S is grounded, and on versions with a VIO or EN pin that pin goes to the +5 V supply as well.
notes: Pin 5 is VIO on the TJA1051T/3 and TJA1051TK/3 and EN on the TJA1051T/E; either goes to VCC. On the TJA1051T pin 5 is unconnected.

circuits.title: Driver symmetry test circuit
circuits.description: A 250 kHz square wave into TXD. CANH and CANL are joined by two 30 Ω resistors in series, and CSPLIT, 4.7 nF, runs from their midpoint to ground. VCC and VIO are supplied.

operation.text: Physical-layer interface between a CAN protocol controller and a two-wire high-speed CAN bus, for automotive use. It meets ISO 11898-2:2003 and ISO 11898-5:2007, and carries the loop-delay symmetry timings that ISO 11898-2:2016 and SAE J2284-4/5 add for CAN FD, so the fast data phase runs at up to 5 Mbit/s. It suits 12 V and 24 V systems. It is meant for nodes that need no standby mode with wake-up over the bus. Its EMC and ESD performance improves on the TJA1050.

Four codes differ only at pin 5. The TJA1051T leaves it unconnected and is a drop-in for the TJA1050. The TJA1051T/3 (SO8) and TJA1051TK/3 (HVSON8, 3.0 mm × 3.0 mm, leadless with improved optical inspection) make it VIO, a logic supply so a 3 V to 5 V microcontroller connects directly. The TJA1051T/E makes it EN, which drops the part into a very low-current Off mode.
S LOW. The driver puts TXD onto CANH and CANL and the differential receiver turns the bus state back into logic on RXD. Bus edge rates are shaped inside the part to keep emissions as low as possible.

S HIGH. The transmitter is off and the bus pins sit recessive; the receiver and everything else keep running, so RXD still follows the bus. It keeps a misbehaving CAN controller from upsetting the whole network.

TJA1051T/E only: EN LOW turns the whole transceiver off to save power when the node has nothing to send or receive. CANH and CANL float, so the node does not load the bus. VCC current is 1 µA to 8 µA.

Each falling edge on TXD starts a timer, and TXD going HIGH clears it. Should TXD remain LOW past tto(dom)TXD (0.3 ms to 5 ms), the transmitter shuts off and the bus falls back to recessive; a stuck pin or a software fault therefore cannot block the bus. Because of this time-out the bit rate cannot go below 20 kbit/s.
Inside the part TXD is pulled up to VIO, while S and the TJA1051T/E's EN are pulled down to GND. A pin left open therefore sits in a defined, safe state.

When VCC falls below Vuvd(VCC) (3.5 V to 4.5 V) or VIO below Vuvd(VIO) (1.3 V to 2.7 V) the transceiver turns off and presents zero load to the bus, and stays so until both supplies are back. Unpowered, the bus pins stay passive, so a node without supply does not disturb the bus.

Above the shutdown junction temperature Tj(sd), 190 °C typ, the bus drivers turn off. They come back once the junction has cooled below Tj(sd) and TXD has returned HIGH; waiting for TXD stops the drivers cycling on and off as the temperature drifts.

On the TJA1051T/3 and TJA1051TK/3, VIO is tied to the microcontroller's supply and sets the thresholds and output level of TXD, RXD and S to match it. On the other versions VIO is joined to VCC inside the part, giving levels for a 5 V microcontroller.

Propagation delays run from TXD crossing 0.3 VTXD (falling) or 0.7 VTXD (rising) to VO(dif) crossing 0.9 V (going dominant) or 0.5 V (going recessive), and on to RXD crossing 0.3 VIO or 0.7 VIO. The loop delays td(TXDL-RXDL) and td(TXDH-RXDH) span TXD to RXD directly. For the bit-width figures TXD sends five dominant bits then one recessive bit of tbit(TXD); tbit(bus) is that recessive bit on the bus between 0.5 V and 0.9 V, and tbit(RXD) the same bit on RXD between 70 % and 30 %.
CANH and CANL withstand ±58 V DC, ±27 V between them, ISO 7637 transient pulses, and ±8 kV ESD both to IEC 61000-4-2 and HBM. Other pins take ±4 kV HBM.

In the HVSON8 the die ground reaches both pin 2 and the exposed pad. Pin 2 has to be soldered to the board's ground; soldering the pad to ground too gives better thermal and electrical performance. Rth(vj-a) is 55 K/W in HVSON8 against 155 K/W in SO8.

Qualified to AEC-Q100 Rev-G for automotive use; halogen free and RoHS compliant. All pins carry ESD protection for normal handling; JESD625-A precautions apply. Leadless packages with lands under the body cannot be wave soldered; peak reflow temperatures follow J-STD-020D by package thickness and volume, and the moisture-sensitivity instructions on the packing apply.
